newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bishop excommunicates local prosecutor.
newsitem.headline: Russian bishop excommunicates local prosecutor.

text.p: A Russian Orthodox bishop has excommunicated the chief state prosecutor in the Volgograd region of southern Russia for investigating the church's activities, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Monday.

Bishop German said Vyacheslav Shestopalov, an avowed atheist and 30-year veteran of law enforcement, was seeking to compromise the church in an aggressive investigation of clerical documents and activities, the report said.
A spokesman for the prosecutor said he reacted calmly to the punishment as he did not believe he could be excommunicated from something of which he was not a member, Tass said.
Neither man could be reached for comment.

The church is flourishing in Russia following seven decades of communist oppression. Excommunication, excluding believers from sacraments and thus condemning them to hell unless they repent, is usually reserved for particularly heinous offenders.
